target: Fujifilm X-M1 1.50 overlay47 station independent-BSS CPU

roots.behavior: Create independent BSS once; copy configured SSID, band/channel, interval and ATIM; initialize PHY/rates; update target BSS, beacon IEs and timing; arm 20000ms alone timer.
Cancel alone timer; merge candidate capabilities with short-slot bit cleared; copy candidate rates, BSSID and beacon interval; configure target BSS/beacon/timing.
Prepare independent peer record with type0x11 and state0, then enter merge processing.
State9 merge switches BSS, associates peer at state2, publishes connection and enters state10; releases parent channel request.

Select PHY/basic/operational rates from target tables; generate BSSID from three low16 entropy outputs, clear multicast bit and set locally-administered bit; preserve existing generated address; build IBSS/privacy/preamble capabilities.

byte_confirmation.reason: All five roots carry NONMATCHING markers at the source pin; their instruction extents were read from the target image, not accepted solely from C.
distilled_device_contract: 0x16: 80-byte BSS payload with media-state1, operation-mode2, SSID-length3, SSID4, BSSID36, operational-rates44, basic-rates46, station-index48, PHY51, authentication52, encryption53, available-PHY54, local-MAC55 and radio-band/channel65/66.

0x1c: action1 uploads beacon information elements only. Header payload action0, network-index1, capabilities4, IE-length6, IEs8. Stock builder strips the 36-byte management/fixed header before upload. Action2 stops beacon transmission with a six-byte payload.
0x19: creation timing payload8, beacon-interval2 and ATIM4. 0x1a: merge timing payload12, association-id2, beacon-interval4 and ATIM6.

0x17: peer-state payload40, index0, type1, MAC2, AID8, listen-interval10, network12, PHY13, desired-rates14, operational-rates16, QoS18, UAPSD-support19, state20, MCS21/22, AMPDU23, HT-capabilities24, HT-extended26, beamforming28, antenna-selection32, opaque station3d metadata33, response-request34, UAPSD35 and service-period36.

Shared peer body serialization accepts canonical NetIndex, PeerIndex and PeerState from vendor_wireless_peers. The association parent supplies the allocated pool lease index; IBSS has no implicit peer-slot0. Secondary callers can request the raw40-byte command body below their owned transport header/sequence engine.

Source-bound peer kinds: independent0x11, secondary client0x22 (write0x012f76dc..0x012f76e0), access point0x41 and P2P access point0x42 (choice0x012f5a2c..0x012f5a58). The secondary access-point setup does not establish a0x21 peer kind.
0x18: peer removal payload8, station-index0 and MAC2.

0x1d: 16-byte radio update, also embedded at BSS payload64. Network0, band1, primary-channel2, secondary-channel3, ERP-protection4, HT-protection5, non-greenfield6, RIFS-protection7, basic-STBC8, operation-protection10, operation-information12, short-preamble13, short-slot14 and fixed0x72 at15.

0x21: EDCA payload44, four records10 bytes each: contention-min0, contention-max2, TXOP4, AIFSN6 as little-endian u16, reserved8 and admission-required9. Station network-index40, QoS41, reserved42/43. Stock untouched padding is initialized to zero.

Independent merge admission uses scan-record0x59 produced from RX descriptor byte5 bit3 at0x012f0ca4..0x012f0cc0. A different BSSID needs that physical indication; this is not a comparison against a fabricated local TSF. The association parent owns admission and physical RX metadata.
Alone timeout0x012dcdb4 releases parent channel and transitions state8 to search1. Timer scheduling and actual scanning belong to the association parent.

ownership.shared_engines: Parent owns entropy acquisition, timer identities/20000ms scheduling, stale physical completion tokens, channel request/release, scan selection, HT/WMM negotiation and network publication. This engine consumes typed entropy, negotiated peer parameters and BssRadioParameters and emits concrete device packets or closed timer/publication/search effects. The same BSS/radio/timing/peer-removal/EDCA serializers are exposed to the infrastructure association parent; the canonical StationElements engine projects negotiated HT operation into BssRadioParameters.
ownership.peer_identity: vendor_wireless_peers owns PeerIndex, NetIndex, PeerState and PeerPool. IBSS imports those types without aliases or reexports. Merge requires an explicitly supplied caller-owned peer index; successful removal clears it. ready_for_merge exposes the exact merge admission predicate, and set_peer rejects replacement throughout an in-progress merge, including gaps between physical commands. The raw peer body and framed command share one field encoder.
ownership.physical_failures: Failed commands return the physical error, retain the first failure and expose stop-beacon/peer-removal/BSS-disconnect cleanup. Failed disconnect does not report an inactive device. No automatic command retry or fake device success is introduced.
ownership.compatibility_correction: Stock assertion loops and fire-and-forget submission become explicit errors and completion-gated publication. Recreating a torn-down BSS retains its generated address; fresh construction requires caller-supplied entropy.

synthetic_test_provenance: Tests construct independent beacon bytes and explicit wire expectations from the distilled X-M1 layouts. No captured frame, firmware bytes or proprietary source is redistributed.
verification: Behavioral tests written but not run. No build, formatter, lint, native runner, SDK, emulator or camera operation was performed. Source inspection and objdump reads are the evidence; runtime qualification belongs to the integration owner.
